   Guide to City Council Proceedings
Meetings of the City Council are held the first and third Tuesday of each month at 9:00 a.m. and are
conducted in accordance with Rosenberg's Rules of Order (Vernon Municipal Code Section 2.04.020).

Copies of all agenda items and back-up materials are available for review in the City Clerk Department,
Vernon City Hall, 4305 Santa Fe Avenue, Vernon, California, and are available for public inspection
during regular business hours, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Agenda reports may be
reviewed on the City's website at www.cityofvernonca.gov or copies may be purchased for $0.20 per
page.

Disability-related services are available to enable persons with a disability to participate in this
meeting, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). In compliance with ADA, if you need
special assistance, please contact the City Clerk department at CityClerk@cityofvernonca.gov or (323)
583-8811 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to assure arrangements can be made.

The general Public Comment portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which
are not listed on the agenda but are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Consent
Calendar and Closed Session. The City Council cannot take action on any item that is not on the
agenda, but matters raised under Public Comment may be referred to staff or scheduled on a future
agenda. Public Comment for Public Hearings and New Business items will be heard during the
consideration of the item. Comments are limited to three minutes per speaker unless a different time limit
is announced. Speaker slips are available at the entrance to the Council Chamber.

Public Hearings are legally noticed hearings. For hearings involving zoning matters, the applicant and
appellant will be given 15 minutes to present their position to the City Council. Time may be set aside for
rebuttal. All other testimony shall follow the rules as set for under Public Comment. If you challenge any
City action in court, you may be limited to raising only those issues you or someone else raised during
the public hearing, or in written correspondence delivered to the City Clerk at or prior to the public
hearing.

Consent Calendar items may be approved by a single motion. If a Council Member or the public wishes
to discuss an item, it may be removed from the calendar for individual consideration. Council Members
may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the
motion to adopt the Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up
following action on the Consent Calendar. Public speakers shall follow the guidelines as set forth under
Public Comment.

New Business items are matters appearing before the Council for the first time for formal action. Those
wishing to address the Council on New Business items shall follow the guidelines for Public Comment.

Closed Session allows the Council to discuss specific matters pursuant to the Brown Act, Government
Code Section 54956.9. Based on the advice of the City Attorney, discussion of these matters in open
session would prejudice the position of the City. The public can comment on Closed Session matters
during the general Public Comment portion of the meeting. Following Closed Session, the City Attorney
will provide an oral report on any reportable matters discussed and actions taken. At the conclusion of
Closed Session, the Council may continue any item listed on the Closed Session agenda to the Open
Session agenda for discussion or to take formal action as it deems appropriate.

  Composting Facility at 2550 27th Street
  Recommendation: A. Conduct a Public Hearing; B. Find that the proposed project
  is categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review
  pursuant to Class 32 In-Fill Developments (CEQA Guidelines 15332) and there is
  no substantial evidence demonstrating that an exception to categorical exemption
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section 15300.2 applies, as the project is consistent
  with the general plan, and the zoning code, the property is less than five (5) acres
  in size and is surrounded by compatible industrial uses, has no value as habitat
  for endangered, rare or threatened species, no significant adverse impacts from
  traffic, parking, noise, dust, dust, air quality, or water quality are expected to occur
  from this project, and the site can be adequately served by all required utilities and
  public services; and C. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-038 approving a Conditional
  Use Permit allowing Dyrt Labs, Inc to operate an indoor food waste composting
  facility at 2550 27th Street and making certain findings as necessary.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra opened the public hearing at 9:17 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:17 a.m.

  Mayor Ybarra invited further Council discussion. Council Member Larios inquired
  how hazardous materials would be handled and how the proposed facility would
  differ from existing waste management facilities. Public Works Director Wall
  responded that the facility would only accept organic materials.

  Health and Environmental Control Director Petrosyan also reassured Council that
  the Health Department would be conducting quarterly inspections. Staff would
  inform Council if any hazardous materials were to be brought in during any future
  instances.

  Lee Robinson of Dyrt Labs, Inc provided a summary of the operations of the
  proposed facility. He announced that all composting would be “in-vessel aerobic
  composting” and most of the waste would be provided by food distributors already
  located within city boundaries.

18.  Regular Vernon City Council Meeting Times
  Recommendation: Discuss meeting times for regular meetings of the City Council
  and provide direction to staff regarding potential changes.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report and provided options for
  Regular City Council meeting times. Mayor Ybarra said she would like to try
  different times during a test period. Council Member Larios said she would like to
  see more candidates apply for City Council, and that a later meeting time would
  allow more public participation and more council candidates. Council Member
  Merlo added that she would want business representatives to be able to attend
  public meetings.

  City Attorney Moussa-Milward added that the City Council should try to minimize
  the test period because certain items cannot be approved during special meetings.
  Discussion ensued among the City Council.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments.

  Marisa Olguin, President of the Vernon Chamber of Commerce, noted that holding
  meetings at 4 p.m. would facilitate attendance from the business community and
  allow residents to engage.

  The City Council agreed to move forward with the test meeting times, including
  one special meeting a month at 4:00 p.m. to gauge engagement.

  City Administrator Saeki clarified Council’s test period requirements: 1) Each first
  meeting of the month would be a special meeting beginning at 4:00 p.m., and the
  second meeting of each month would remain at 9:00 a.m. 2) Information regarding
  the testing period would be brought back for Council consideration during the
  second City Council meeting in January. 3) The testing period would commence in
  September or October, pending a final review of upcoming business items from
  staff.

  Mayor Ybarra invited additional public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra
  called for a motion.

Background
The Malburg Generating Station (MGS) requires a dedicated Data Acquisition and Handling
System (DAHS) to ensure continuous compliance with the South Coast Air Quality Management
District (SCAQMD) and the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA).

SCAQMD mandates minute-by-minute monitoring under Rules 218.2 and 218.3. At the federal
level, the facility must comply with Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 75,
which requires emissions data to be formatted and transmitted directly to the US EPA's web-
based Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) platform.

Currently, MGS utilizes RegPerfect software by Teledyne Monitor Labs (Teledyne) as its DAHS
to comply with SCAQMD and U.S. EPA requirements. RegPerfect ensures that emissions remain
within permit limits and tracks data and errors to prevent deviations that could lead to fines. By
automatically executing required functions and generating formatted electronic data reports, the
RegPerfect system communicates MGS’s physical stack sensor data to regulatory databases
with minimal operator intervention.

In early 2026, the U.S. EPA modernized its ECMPS platform by transitioning to ECMPS 2.0,
which includes significant updates to architectural, data format, and security. As a result of this
migration, the legacy ECMPS version used by MGS is no longer compatible. To upgrade to a
compatible version of RegPerfect, MGS must reconfigure and update its server as well as its
programmable logic controllers (PLCs).

The proposed Purchase Contract is exempt from competitive bidding and competitive selection
pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) Sections 3.32.110(A)(2) and 3.32.110(B)(1)
respectively, because Teledyne is the original equipment manufacturer of the RegPerfect
software and owns the proprietary matching monitoring hardware. Teledyne possesses the
specialized technical expertise necessary to perform this critical compliance upgrade. Engaging
a different, compliant DAHS platform from another vendor would require a significant overhaul of
our system, leading to extended plant outages, prolonged testing periods, and formal
recertification of the MGS permit with the SCAQMD.

Subject

Recommendation
A. Pursuant to Sections 3.32.220(B) and 3.32.110(B)(3) of the Vernon Municipal Code (VMC),
find that it is commercially unreasonable to rebid the existing services agreement with SDI
Presence LLC as necessary project implementations have not yet been completed; and
B. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute Amendment No. 3 to the Professional
Services Agreement with SDI Presence LLC, in substantially the same form as submitted,
extending the agreement for project management services for an additional one (1) year through
August 19, 2027, with no increase in compensation.

Background
On April 20, 2021, City Council approved the Services agreement with SDI Presence LLC for
project management services for Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system implementation
in an amount not to exceed $819,000 for three (3) years. The funds for a project management
consultant were approved by City Council on December 1, 2020, with the approval of the ERP
Software system with Tyler Technologies, Inc. Since the inception of the contract, SDI has
served as the project management consultant for the implementation of several modules in Tyler
Technologies Enterprise ERP (formerly Munis) and Enterprise Permitting & Licensing (formerly
EnerGov).

Amendment No. 1 was approved by City Council on August 1, 2023, for an additional
$224,437.50 and extended the agreement to August 19, 2025. Despite completing the
implementation of several modules, unexpected implementation challenges caused project
delays and created a need for additional assistance beyond August 2025. Therefore,
Amendment No. 2 was approved by the City Administrator on July 28, 2025, extending the
agreement for an additional year through August 19, 2026. To date, the contract has a remaining
balance of $182,700 and SDI’s services are still needed to continue with necessary upcoming
ERP module implementations.

The implementation of the Accounts Receivable/General Billing (AR/GB) module was placed on
hold in fiscal year 2025-26 as City Departments, including the Fiber Optics (Fiber) division of
Public Utilities, continued to use Eden for billing. Eden is expected to reach end of life and be
unsupported after March 2027. After the completion of the current utility billing system upgrade
in October 2025, it was determined that CIS version 5 (CISv5) can in fact support Fiber billing.
Transition of the Fiber billing to CISv5 is underway and expected to go live before Eden reaches
end of life. Having this confirmation from the Public Utilities department, implementation of
AR/GB can restart since we no longer have to bring all the Fiber customers and open items into
Munis.

Subject
Donation to Vernon City Elementary School for Interventionist Position

Recommendation
A. Find that providing financial support to Vernon City Elementary School (VCES) serves a public
purpose and benefits Vernon area students;
B. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute a donation letter, in substantially the
same form as submitted, memorializing the City of Vernon’s commitment to funding the
Interventionist position at VCES for a total amount not-to-exceed $174,349 for the 2026-27
school year; and
C. Authorize the City Administrator to make additional donations to VCES in an amount up to
$25,651 for the specific purpose of funding the Interventionist position for the 2026-27 school
year, should the final compensation amount for the position exceed $174,349. Total donations
to VCES for this purpose shall not exceed the $200,000 allocated by City Council in the City’s
budget for Fiscal Year 2026-27.

Background
As part of the City’s Strategic Planning process, the City Council received input from residents
and stakeholders regarding community needs and used the feedback to establish future goals
and priorities. During this process, the school administration of Vernon City Elementary School
(VCES) shared the challenges they would face in their efforts to provide high-quality education
and support for its students with crucial funding for the school falling short of expectations for the
upcoming school year. The City Council’s desire to aid the school’s efforts to maintain critical
staff positions for the 2026-27 school year was identified as Task 1.9 of the 2026-2031 Strategic
Plan under the goal to Strengthen City Credibility and Partnerships.

Subsequently, during the City’s budget process for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27, the City Council
received a request from VCES to fund the Interventionist position at the school for the 2026-27
school year. VCES is a public K-6 school within the Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD)
and is the only school located within the City’s boundaries. The school serves students who live
in and around the City as well as students whose parents work at the businesses located in the
City. The school’s Principal indicated that due to LAUSD’s budgetary constraints and without
another funding source, the school would lose an on-site Interventionist for the 2026-27 school
year. After considering the critical academic support services provided by the Interventionist and
the need at VCES, the City Council authorized a one-time allocation of $200,000 to be used to
support the Interventionist position during the 2026-27 school year. The proposed donation letter
memorializes the City’s commitment to its partnership with VCES and LAUSD in promoting
educational excellence and providing students with the resources and academic support needed
to succeed.

Donation Letter
LAUSD’s rules for receiving donations allow for donors to stipulate that the donation should be
used.  for a specific purpose or program only. Accordingly, the proposed donation letter
(Attachment
  .  1) specifically indicates the following:

Interventionist Position
The Interventionist provides direct services to students in multiple content areas and participates
in the implementation of a Multi-tiered System of Support (MTSS) that includes intervention via
re-teaching and professional development of teachers. The Interventionist provides direct
targeted instruction and intervention for students, collaborates and co-plans with other teachers
to share effective instructional practices, and supports community engagement and parent
involvement. The primary duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Interventionist job flyer
(Attachment 2). Maria Nercessian has served as the Interventionist at VCES and would continue
to serve in that capacity for the 2026-27 school year if funding for the position is available.

Request to Utilize Remaining Funds
As the letter reads currently, the funds are to be used exclusively for the Interventionist position.
The amount of $174,349 provided by VCES for the cost to fund the position for the 2026-27
school year is based on the pay scale and salary basis of the incumbent and includes base
salary, non-wage labor costs, and health/medical benefits (Attachment 3). Although it is not
anticipated that the position will cost less than this amount, VCES has requested that if it does,
any remaining funds be allowed to be spent on the purchase of interventionist instructional
materials and resources. Should City Council determine that is acceptable, the language in bold
below would be added to the letter:

  “The funds shall be used exclusively to support the interventionist position, including
  salary, benefits, applicable fringe costs, and, if permitted under LAUSD fiscal policies
  and procedures, any remaining funds may be used to purchase instructional
  materials and resources that directly support the Interventionist position and
  student intervention services.”

Authority for Additional Donations
In the event that the cost of funding the Interventionist position at VCES during the 2026-27
school year exceeds the $174,349, staff is requesting that the City Administrator be authorized
to make additional donations to the school for this sole specific purpose up to an amount of
$25,651. The total amount of donations to VCES for this purpose would not exceed the $200,000
allocated by City Council in the City’s budget for FY 2026-27. If approved by City Council, staff
would proceed with the initial donation disbursement of $174,349 to VCES. Any subsequent
requests for additional funding up to $25,651 for the sole purpose of supporting the Interventionist
position would be subject to approval by the City Administrator and memorialized in separate
donation letters to be reviewed and approved as-to-form by the City Attorney.
